core_principle: Attacker-controlled input causes a privileged component to act on the attacker's behalf, crossing a trust boundary that should separate the attacker from the privileged capability. The component has authority the attacker lacks — network position, file system access, credentials, or elevated permissions. The attacker does not gain the component's identity; they gain the component's capability by controlling its actions.

minimum_causal_signature.authority_transition: Attacker supplies data specifying an operation or destination; the privileged component executes the operation using its own ambient authority (network position, local socket, or IAM role), granting privileged execution to untrusted intent.
minimum_causal_signature.security_decision_bypassed: The protected destination relies on ambient positional trust (evaluating caller source address or caller process identity) rather than authenticating the initiator of the request.
minimum_causal_signature.failure_condition: Attacker-controlled data determines the target or operation of a privileged sink without strict allowlist validation, enabling the server's ambient authority to be exerted on arbitrary targets.

conditions: A component has authority the attacker lacks (network position, credentials, file access, elevated permissions)
Attacker-controlled input influences what the privileged component does (destination, command, resource path)

The trust boundary between the attacker and the capability is not enforced at the input layer — the component acts on the input without verifying whether the attacker should have the resulting capability
investigation_question: Can attacker-controlled input cause a privileged component to perform an action the attacker could not perform directly? What capability does the attacker gain — and what authority makes that capability possible?
defensive_implication: Validate attacker-controlled input against a strict allowlist before passing it to any privileged component. The validation must constrain the action to only those operations the attacker is authorized to trigger. Apply defense-in-depth at the infrastructure layer — assume the application-level validation may be bypassed and limit the privileged component's own capabilities (network segmentation, least-privilege IAM roles, disabled metadata endpoints).
common_manifestations: SSRF: Attacker controls the destination of a server-side HTTP request, gaining the server's network position
XXE with external entities: XML parser fetches attacker-controlled URLs using the server's file/network access
PDF generators that fetch attacker-controlled URLs using the server's network position
Headless browsers (Chromium, wkhtmltopdf) rendering attacker-controlled URLs from the server's network

sources.title: PortSwigger - Server-side request forgery (SSRF)
sources.claim: SSRF attacks exploit trust relationships to escalate an attack from the vulnerable application and perform unauthorized actions, leveraging trust relationships with the server or back-end systems

sources.title: OWASP - Server Side Request Forgery
sources.claim: SSRF allows an attacker to abuse server functionality to perform requests to internal/external resources on behalf of the server
